header.title: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicitas: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Martyrium Perpetuae et Felcitatis
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg2016.tlg001.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2016.tlg001.1st1K-gr: “Except one [at a time]”: the text reads μοσχὸν ἕνα (“one calf”), apparently a corruption of μόνον ἕνα (“only one”). “Ask for visions … receive a vision” renders the doubled ὀπτασίας ὀπτασίαν, which may be a dittography.

nodes.text: Then my brother said to me: “Lady sister, you are already in great honour, so great that if you were to ask for visions you would receive a vision, to have it shown to you whether you are to have a reprieve or are going to suffer.” And I, who knew that I talked with God, from whom I had received so many kindnesses, being full of faith, promised him, saying: “Tomorrow I will tell you.” I asked, and this was shown to me. I saw a bronze ladder of wonderful length, whose length reached up to heaven; and it was narrow, so that no one could climb up by it except one [at a time]; and on both sides of the ladder every kind of sword, spear, hook, knife and spit was fixed there, so that anyone climbing carelessly and without looking up would have his flesh torn by the points. And under the ladder itself there was a huge serpent, which lay in wait for those climbing, terrifying them so that they would not dare to climb. Saturus went up, he who later gave himself up of his own will for our sake, for we were his building; but when we were arrested he was absent. When he reached the top of the ladder, he turned and said: “Perpetua, I am waiting for you; but take care that the serpent does not bite you.” And I said: “He will not harm me, in the name of Jesus Christ.” And from beneath the ladder, as if afraid of me, he slowly put out his head; and as I meant to step onto the first rung, I trod on his head. And I saw there a very large garden, and in the middle of the garden a grey-haired man of great size sitting, in the dress of a shepherd, who was milking the sheep; and around him stood many thousands clothed in white. Raising his head, he looked at me and said: “You are welcome, child.” And he called me, and from the cheese which he was milking he gave me as it were a morsel; and I took it with my hands joined and ate; and all who stood by said: “Amen.” And at the sound of the voice I woke, still chewing something sweet. And at once I told my brother, and we understood that [I] must suffer; and from then on I began to have no hope in this world.
